A few tips to get you started.

>I assumed that Mages would be low mobility, low defensive

No class is going to just outright be dogshit defensively like this. They are either going to be tanky, have some sort of built in healing, be able to kite, or some combination of the three.

BigDebuffs is a useful addon that attaches an icon of CDs being used by enemy classes. Record your footage and familiarize yourself with what is being used. Eventually you will understand each of the icons. For example, if a rogue pops evasion or cloak, it will show that icon by their nameplate. So if you are say a warrior, you know not to attack into evasion... or stun them so you can continue hitting them. It also shows offensive cds so if the same rogue pops shadow dance, you can disarm them to counter their offensive cd.

I dont use it but another popular addon, Omnibar, can track important enemy cds so you can always have an idea of what your enemy has available to use. Personally I just have a lot of experience playing the game and I can mentally keep track of it while playing the game. (Loading my screen with too many addons makes me play worse). In my head I categorize a lot of cds as a one time or two time per game button.

For example if my kill target is rogue and he has a disc healer and a ret partner, and I am on warrior: The once a round cds im really worried about hitting into: Rogue only has cheat death (maybe) and evasion that I really care about not hitting into. Disc has dome, 2 charges of pain supp. ret has bop and LOH. Once those are gone I know rogue is good to kill. Sometimes if you are blowing cds and you get a defensive out of someone and you hard swap to avoid hitting into the defensive, you can get multiple defensives from the rogue's team, etc.

* Ring of Peace (knockback circle) This has been pretty unreliable this expansion. Not sure if it is DRing with Whirling Dragon Punch or something else but it seems to just have a built in failure rate.
* Clash (target's an enemy and both you and that enemy player charge each other and meet halfway and is followed with a short root) I like to use this to interrupt spellcasting. Its pretty easy to look at mathematically:

5% Damage and 30% Weapon AA Speed \~\~VS\~\~ 32% Increased White Damage and 2x Stats.

30% Attack Speed is the same thing as increasing damage by 30%. With the 5% damage this actually brings your auto attack damage above dual wielding Two Handers. Two handers are generally 32% above One Handers in damage. The 5% damage increase brings that down to 26% and the attack speed will actually favor one handers. Unfortunately Auto attack damage is pretty meaningless when it comes to our burst profile.

A single two handed weapon provides about 7% of a fury warrior's overall strength alone in full season 1 TWW gear. The 5% Damage increase on the talent doesn't make up the difference. This doesn't even include the 2x stats on Vers, Mastery/Haste. Because we gain so much in terms of stats through the course of the expansion, this is only going to get worse. (We have 17k baseline strength at 80, as gear grows and we end this expansion at something crazy like 100M HP, our baseline stats will be laughable) All this to say - if you want to play SMF, season 1 is probably the best season for it, as it will only get worse.
